findings.reason: a node can implement the plan write once per call instead of once per move, pass this gate on the single-move fixture, and leave five of the six measured disagreements in place.
findings.text: the done-when's fixture performs a single move, while §8's own "Why" measures six plans moved in one portfolio operation and its refusal clause is stated batch-wide ("refuses the whole call and writes nothing"), so it names neither the batch that motivated the section nor a second move op in the fixture

findings.reason: the deliverable is stated generally ("A sprint move writes the plan's sprint"), so as written the plan implies a coverage it does not have; it must either name `_move_sprint_item` as in scope or state that it is retired, otherwise the defect persists on a callable path.
findings.text: §8 locates the fix in `edit_plan` alone ("the `move` batch is applied by `edit_plan` in `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py` … so the change goes there"), but the same module holds a second, independent implementer of the same sprint move, `_move_sprint_item` (reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:566), which writes the index through `write_plan(project, "index", …)` and never touches the plan's `sprint`; it is exported onto the MCP namespace (reckon/mcp.py:221) and pinned by tests/test_mcp_tools.py:421/445/464

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_apply_move` resolves in `reckon/_store.py` (:3404) and is index-only exactly as claimed; `edit_plan` resolves as the registered tool (reckon/mcp.py:3205) over `_edit_plan` (:1070) and `_edit_plan_tool` (:1653); `tests/test_edit_plan.py` names a file that exists.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's gate builds its fixture from one move and one refusal, while the measurement the same section cites is a six-plan move ("six plans moved between sprints"), so the batch case that motivated the section is not exercised.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8's logs sit "under the run directory", the per-run crew directory on GPFS that survives the run, not a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test name and the symbols §8 names carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and no comment narrates a prior state of the code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8's mechanism names one of two writers of a sprint move in `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py`, so `_move_sprint_item` keeps the defect §8 states it fixes.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable (a sprint move writes the moved plan's `plan-sprint`); its move, refusal and §4-membership assertions are three faces of that one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §6 declares `plan-section-depends-on: {s6: [the-portfolio-reads-true#s8]}` (plan.html:29), the roadmap resolves that mapping into per-section edges (reckon/roadmap.py:452, :4021) so §6's S22 re-sprint is held until §8 lands, and §8 needs no dependency of its own because it writes only `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py` and its own new test file.
